lines.text: name: unslop

lines.author: matemolnar8
lines.text: description: Cut AI tells from any writing. Must always apply.

lines.author: Máté Molnár
lines.text: disable-model-invocation: true

lines.author: matemolnar8
lines.text: # Unslop

lines.author: Máté Molnár
lines.text: Edit text to remove AI patterns.

lines.author: matemolnar8
lines.text: ## Process

lines.author: matemolnar8
lines.text: 1. Scan for the patterns below.

lines.author: matemolnar8
lines.text: 2. Rewrite. Preserve meaning, match intended tone.

lines.author: Máté Molnár
lines.text: 3. Self-audit: "What makes this obviously AI generated?" Fix remaining tells.

lines.author: matemolnar8
lines.text: ## Patterns to detect and fix

lines.author: Máté Molnár
lines.text: Rule numbers are stable ids that other skills cite. A removed rule leaves a gap.

lines.author: matemolnar8
lines.text: ### Content

lines.author: matemolnar8
lines.text: 3. **Superficial -ing phrases.** "highlighting...", "ensuring...", "reflecting...", "showcasing...", "fostering...". Delete or expand with real sources.

lines.author: matemolnar8
lines.text: 5. **Vague attributions.** "Experts believe", "Industry reports suggest", "Some critics argue". Name the source or delete.

lines.author: matemolnar8
lines.text: ### Language

lines.author: matemolnar8
lines.text: 7. **AI vocabulary.** Additionally, crucial, delve, enduring, enhance, fostering, garner, interplay, intricate, landscape (abstract), pivotal, showcase, tapestry (abstract), testament, underscore, vibrant. Replace with plain words.

lines.author: matemolnar8
lines.text: 8. **Fancy ways to say "is".** "serves as", "stands as", "boasts", "features". Just say "is" or "has".

lines.author: matemolnar8
lines.text: 9. **"Not just X, but Y."** State the point directly instead.

lines.author: matemolnar8
lines.text: 10. **Rule of three.** Forcing ideas into groups of three. Use the natural number.

lines.author: matemolnar8
lines.text: 11. **Synonym cycling.** Protagonist, main character, central figure, hero all in one paragraph. Pick one, repeat it.

lines.author: matemolnar8
lines.text: 12. **False ranges.** "from X to Y" where X and Y aren't on a meaningful scale. List topics directly.

lines.author: matemolnar8
lines.text: ### Style

lines.author: Máté Molnár
lines.text: 13. **Em dash overuse.** Avoid em dashes entirely. Use periods or commas only (no parentheses, no en dashes, no hyphen-as-dash substitutes). If a thought needs separation, end the sentence or use a comma.

lines.author: matemolnar8
lines.text: 14. **Colon overuse.** Colons are fine before a list or example. Not as mid-sentence connectors. "If you're coming from traditional automation: instead of registering event handlers, you describe conditions" adds nothing with the colon. Rewrite to let the point stand on its own without comparison framing. "Describing when the scheduler should fire works best as plain English." Same meaning, no crutch punctuation.

lines.author: matemolnar8
lines.text: 15. **Boldface overuse.** Don't bold every proper noun or acronym.

lines.author: matemolnar8
lines.text: 16. **Inline-header lists.** The tell is a bold label and colon that restates the line: "**Performance:** Performance improved...". Convert those to prose. A bold lead-in that ends in a period, names the item, and is followed by genuinely new detail ("**Schema in TypeScript.** Tables live in one file.") is fine, not a tell.

lines.author: matemolnar8
lines.text: 17. **Title case headings.** Use sentence case.

lines.author: matemolnar8
lines.text: 18. **Decorative emojis.** Remove from headings and bullets.

lines.author: matemolnar8
lines.text: 19. **Curly quotes.** Replace with straight quotes.

lines.author: matemolnar8
lines.text: ### Communication artifacts

lines.author: matemolnar8
lines.text: 20. **Chatbot phrases.** "I hope this helps!", "Let me know if...", "Of course!", "Certainly!", "Found the smoking gun!" Remove.

lines.author: matemolnar8
lines.text: 22. **Sycophantic tone.** "Great question! You're absolutely right!" Respond directly.

lines.author: matemolnar8
lines.text: ### Filler

lines.author: matemolnar8
lines.text: 23. **Filler phrases.** "In order to" becomes "To". "Due to the fact that" becomes "Because". "It is important to note that" gets deleted.

lines.author: matemolnar8
lines.text: 24. **Excessive hedging.** "could potentially possibly be argued that it might" becomes "may".

lines.author: matemolnar8
lines.text: 25. **Generic conclusions.** "The future looks bright." State specific plans or facts.

lines.author: matemolnar8
lines.text: ### Jargon

lines.author: matemolnar8
lines.text: 26. **Abstract metaphor nouns.** Substrate, wedge, vector, locus, vantage, nexus, primitive (as noun), harness (as metaphor), surface (as in "API surface"), bedrock, scaffolding (as metaphor), modality, paradigm, gold-plating, ratchet (as metaphor), evacuate (for moving code), endgame, north star, flywheel. These read as technical but usually have a plainer concrete word. "Substrate" becomes "base". "Wedge in" becomes "add". "Vector" becomes "way" or "method". "Gold-plating" becomes "more than the job needs". "Ratchet" becomes the mechanism's real name or "a limit that only tightens". "Evacuate" becomes "move out". "Endgame" becomes "the last phase". Pick the concrete word.

lines.author: matemolnar8
lines.text: ### Plain speech

lines.author: matemolnar8
lines.text: 27. **Say what it does, not how it feels.** "the database stays close at hand", "SQL you can read", "types that follow your schema" name a feeling. The fix names the mechanism or a number: "`.toSQL()` returns the exact string sent to the database", "a column rename fails the build". Ask what the sentence tells the reader to do or know, then write that. If you can't restate it as a concrete instruction, fact, or number, cut it. One more check: if the sentence could appear unchanged in another project's docs, it says nothing about this one. Cut it.

lines.author: matemolnar8
lines.text: 28. **Shorten or split dense sentences.** If the reader has to backtrack to parse a sentence, break it in two or drop clauses. One idea per sentence.

lines.author: matemolnar8
lines.text: 29. **Active voice.** Prefer it. Catch "is/are/was/were + past participle" and name the actor: "queries are validated" becomes "the compiler validates queries", "the file is parsed by the loader" becomes "the loader parses the file". Passive is fine only when the actor is unknown or genuinely doesn't matter.

lines.author: matemolnar8
lines.text: 30. **Cut adverbs, or use a stronger verb.** "runs quickly" becomes "is fast" or the number. "significantly improves" becomes the measured delta. An adverb propping up a weak verb means the verb is wrong.

lines.author: matemolnar8
lines.text: 31. **Prefer the plain word.** "utilize" becomes "use", "leverage" becomes "use", "facilitate" becomes "help", "numerous" becomes "many", "in the event that" becomes "if". The fancier synonym is rarely clearer.

lines.author: Máté Molnár
lines.text: 32. **Mannered prose.** Metaphor or flourish where a literal phrase exists: aphorisms ("wire it or delete it"), rhetorical fragments for effect, personified code ("the plan holds it"), figurative verbs ("rides along", "stands on"), stock framing phrases. "A dial worth turning" becomes "a parameter worth varying". Say what you mean. Rule 26 covers the metaphor nouns.

lines.author: Máté Molnár
lines.text: 33. **Over-compression.** Dropped articles, verbless fragments, symbol-speak, and abbreviations that make the reader decode instead of read. "Parser rejects bad date → exit 2, no write" becomes "The parser rejects a bad date, exits with code 2, and writes nothing." Write whole sentences with their articles and verbs, and spell out arrows and abbreviations.
